picks.reasoning: Championship leaders Middlesbrough enter on an 11-match unbeaten league run with 30 goals scored across 13 games, fresh off a 3-0 rout of Charlton Athletic powered by a second consecutive brace from striker Will Lankshear and having already defeated Wrexham in the Carabao Cup this season. By contrast, 18th-placed Wrexham have won just three of 13 league fixtures, suffered back-to-back defeats without scoring, and lost striker Sam Smith to a long-term knee injury alongside attacking doubts Callum O'Hare, Josh Windass, and Nathan Broadhead. Ladbrokes' 1.73 price (57.8% implied) significantly undervalues Boro against our 69.0% true win projection.

Third-placed Wolverhampton Wanderers have surged into automatic promotion contention with 10 points from their last four matches, arriving off a dominant 3-0 victory over Cardiff City with Fer López and Adam Armstrong in fine scoring touch. Meanwhile, 14th-placed Bristol City have lost four of their six home fixtures at Ashton Gate while managing just three home league goals all season, and striker Lorent Tolaj remains hampered by a hip injury. At 2.20 (45.5% implied), Ladbrokes underprice Wolves' superior firepower against our 56.5% true away win estimate.

Cesc Fàbregas's Como have won five consecutive matches across all competitions and sit 9th in the Champions League league phase after statement 4-1 victories over RB Leipzig and Manchester United, with rested playmaker Martin Baturina returning alongside Nico Paz and Anastasios Douvikas. Conversely, 27th-placed RC Lens have suffered back-to-back Champions League defeats without scoring against Sporting CP (0-2) and Club Brugge (0-3), enter off a 1-0 domestic loss to Lille, and remain without injured forwards Odsonne Edouard and Abdallah Sima. Ladbrokes' 1.95 odds (51.3% implied) underestimate Como's momentum against our 61.7% true win probability.
